exact_citation_checks.quote:
Assume the Axiom of Countable Choice ($\mathrm{AC}_\omega$), inherited from the cited Lebesgue, polar, Newtonian and distribution interfaces ([[def-countable-choice]]).
Work in $\mathbb R^3$ with its Euclidean structure ([[def-euclidean-inner-product]], [[def-metric-ball]]) and the constants of [[def-em-si-conventions]], $\varepsilon_0=(\mu_0c^2)^{-1}>0$.
Let $\Phi$ be the $n=3$ fundamental solution of $-\Delta$ of [[def-laplace-fundamental-solution-with-positive-minus-laplacian-sign]], normalised by $-\Delta T_\Phi=\delta_0$; then $\omega_2=4\pi$ and
$$\Phi(z)=\frac{1}{4\pi|z|}\qquad(z\ne0)$$
([[cor-volume-of-the-unit-n-ball]], [[lem-euclidean-chart-measure-agrees-with-polar-surface-measure]]).
Let $Nf$ be the Newtonian potential of [[def-newtonian-potential]].

(a) [Smooth compact sources] Let $\rho:\mathbb R^3\to\mathbb R$ be of class $C^1$ with compact support contained in $\overline B_R$ ([[def-ck-euclidean-maps-and-diffeomorphisms]], [[def-metric-ball]]), put $\varphi:=\varepsilon_0^{-1}N\rho$ and $E:=-\nabla\varphi$.
Then $\varphi\in C^2(\mathbb R^3)$ ([[thm-newtonian-potential-for-holder-data-is-classical]]), and pointwise on $\mathbb R^3$
$$-\Delta\varphi=\frac{\rho}{\varepsilon_0},\qquad \operatorname{div}E=\frac{\rho}{\varepsilon_0},\qquad \operatorname{curl}E=0$$
with the operators of [[def-laplacian-of-a-c2-function]] and [[def-divergence-and-curl-of-a-c1-vector-field]].
Moreover, with $Q:=\int\rho\,d\lambda_3$, for every $x\in\mathbb R^3$ the absolutely convergent Coulomb integral representation holds, and its far-field bound holds for $|x|>2R$,
$$E(x)=\frac{1}{4\pi\varepsilon_0}\int_{\mathbb R^3}\frac{x-y}{|x-y|^3}\rho(y)\,d\lambda_3(y)\quad(x\in\mathbb R^3),\qquad |E(x)|\le\frac{\| \rho\|_1}{\pi\varepsilon_0|x|^2}\quad(|x|>2R),$$
and for $|x|>\max(2R,1)$ the potential obeys the decay bound $|\varphi(x)|\le\bigl(|Q|/(4\pi)+R\|\rho\|_1/\pi\bigr)/(\varepsilon_0|x|)$ ([[lem-em-newtonian-far-field-gradient]], [[thm-decay-of-the-newtonian-potential-of-compactly-supported-data]]).
The pair $(E,0,\rho,0)$ therefore realises the pure electrostatic regime of [[def-em-electrostatic-regime]] with source $\rho$, and $E$ is the field of the localised Newtonian potential.

(b) [Uniqueness with vanishing at infinity] If $\psi\in C^2(\mathbb R^3)$ satisfies $-\Delta\psi=\rho/\varepsilon_0$ pointwise on $\mathbb R^3$ and $\lim_{|x|\to\infty}\psi(x)=0$, then $\psi=\varphi$ ([[thm-weak-maximum-principle-for-the-laplacian]]).
In particular, among $C^2$ solutions of the Poisson equation of a compactly supported $C^1$ source decaying at infinity, the localised Newtonian potential is the unique one.

(c) [Compactly supported $L^1$ sources] If instead $\rho\in L^1(\mathbb R^3)$ is real, measurable and compactly supported, then $N\rho$ is finite $\lambda_3$-almost everywhere, belongs to $L^1_{\mathrm{loc}}(\mathbb R^3)$, is $C^\infty$ and harmonic off the support of $\rho$, and its regular distribution satisfies
$$-\Delta T_{\varepsilon_0^{-1}N\rho}=T_{\rho/\varepsilon_0}\qquad\text{in }\mathcal D'(\mathbb R^3)$$
([[thm-newtonian-potential-solves-poisson-distributionally]], scaled by $\varepsilon_0^{-1}$; [[def-regular-distribution-from-a-locally-integrable-function]], [[def-distributional-derivative]]).

(d) [Point charge] Let $q\in\mathbb R$ and $x_0\in\mathbb R^3$ and define, with arbitrary values at $x_0$,
$$\varphi_q(x):=\frac{q}{4\pi\varepsilon_0|x-x_0|},\qquad E_q(x):=\frac{q\,(x-x_0)}{4\pi\varepsilon_0|x-x_0|^3}\qquad(x\ne x_0).$$
Then $\varphi_q\in L^1_{\mathrm{loc}}(\mathbb R^3)$, $E_q$ is locally integrable and $C^\infty$ off $x_0$, $E_q=-\nabla\varphi_q$ on $\mathbb R^3\setminus\{x_0\}$, and, with $T_{\varphi_q}$ the regular distribution of $\varphi_q$ and $\operatorname{div}E_q:=\sum_i\partial_iT_{E_{q,i}}$, $\operatorname{curl}E_q:=(\partial_2T_{E_{q,3}}-\partial_3T_{E_{q,2}},\ \partial_3T_{E_{q,1}}-\partial_1T_{E_{q,3}},\ \partial_1T_{E_{q,2}}-\partial_2T_{E_{q,1}})$,
$$-\Delta T_{\varphi_q}=\frac{q}{\varepsilon_0}\delta_{x_0},\qquad \operatorname{div}E_q=\frac{q}{\varepsilon_0}\delta_{x_0},\qquad \operatorname{curl}E_q=0\qquad\text{in }\mathcal D'(\mathbb R^3)$$
([[thm-minus-laplacian-of-the-fundamental-solution-is-dirac]] for the first identity, [[lem-em-distributional-gradient-smooth-off-a-point]] for the passage from the potential to the field, [[def-distributional-derivative]], [[def-dirac-delta-and-its-derivatives]]).
The distribution $q\delta_{x_0}$ is the fixed-time reading of the stationary point charge of [[def-em-weak-sources]](b) with charge parameter $q$ and constant trajectory $z\equiv x_0$ ([[def-em-electrostatic-regime]](e)); so the pair $(E_q,0)$ satisfies the distributional pure electrostatic equations with that point source.
This is an idealised point-source model: no claim of uniqueness for the point source, no self-force and no statement about the field at $x_0$ itself is made.

exact_citation_checks.quote:
**Regularity convention for a possibly non-open parameter interval.** Let $U\subseteq\mathbb R^3$ be open, let $I\subseteq\mathbb R$ be an interval and let $k\in\mathbb N$. A map on $U\times I$ is **jointly $C^k$** when it is the restriction of a $C^k$ map on some open neighbourhood $N\subseteq\mathbb R^4$ of $U\times I$, in the sense of [[def-ck-euclidean-maps-and-diffeomorphisms]]; it is **jointly $C^\infty$** when it is the restriction of one smooth map on such an open neighbourhood. For open $I$ these are exactly the usual open-domain classes; at included endpoints of a nondegenerate interval, time derivatives are the corresponding relative one-sided derivatives. For empty or singleton $I$ the convention still asserts extension existence and the spatial identities below, but it does not determine time jets uniquely from the restricted values alone. The convention does not require a fixed uniform enlargement of an unbounded $I$.

**Vector witness.** Let $U\subseteq\mathbb R^3$ be open and star-shaped with centre $a\in U$ ([[def-star-shaped-open-subset-of-rn]]), let $I\subseteq\mathbb R$ be an interval, let $k\ge1$, and let $B:U\times I\to\mathbb R^3$ be jointly $C^k$ with $\operatorname{div}B(\cdot,t)=0$ on $U$ for every $t\in I$ ([[def-divergence-and-curl-of-a-c1-vector-field]]). Then

$$A(x,t):=\int_0^1s\,B\bigl(a+s(x-a),t\bigr)\times(x-a)\,ds$$

is jointly $C^k$ on $U\times I$ and

$$\operatorname{curl}A(\cdot,t)=B(\cdot,t)\qquad(t\in I),$$

the curl being taken in the spatial variables and the cross product being that of [[def-cross-product-in-r3]].

**Scalar witness.** If in addition $C:U\times I\to\mathbb R^3$ is jointly $C^k$ with $\operatorname{curl}C(\cdot,t)=0$ on $U$ for every $t\in I$, then

$$\phi(x,t):=-\int_0^1\bigl\langle C\bigl(a+s(x-a),t\bigr),\,x-a\bigr\rangle\,ds$$

is jointly $C^k$ on $U\times I$ and

$$\nabla\phi(\cdot,t)=-C(\cdot,t)\qquad(t\in I),$$

the gradient and inner product being those of [[def-directional-and-partial-derivatives]] and [[def-euclidean-inner-product]]. For jointly $C^\infty$ data both potentials are jointly $C^\infty$. No global potential on a non-star-shaped open set is claimed, and the fields $B(\cdot,t)$ and $C(\cdot,t)$ need not be continuous in $t$ at endpoints beyond the stated one-sided convention.

exact_citation_checks.quote:
Let $\Omega\subseteq(-L,L)^3$ be bounded and open, let $\varepsilon$ be a measurable symmetric real $3\times3$ matrix field on $\Omega$ with $\alpha|\xi|^2\le\xi\cdot\varepsilon(x)\xi\le\beta|\xi|^2$ for a.e. $x$ and all $\xi\in\mathbb R^3$, $0<\alpha\le\beta<\infty$, let $G\in H^1(\Omega)$ be a specified lift, and let $F\in(H_0^1(\Omega))^*$ be bounded. Then there is exactly one $u\in G+H_0^1(\Omega)$ with

$$\int_\Omega\nabla v\cdot\varepsilon\nabla u=F(v)\qquad\text{for every }v\in H_0^1(\Omega),$$

where $H_0^1=W_0^{1,2}(\Omega)$ carries the gradient norm. For $F(v)=\int_\Omega\rho v$ with $\rho\in L^2(\Omega)$ this is the weak Poisson solution $-\operatorname{div}(\varepsilon\nabla u)=\rho$, with the homogeneous boundary datum represented by membership of $H_0^1$ rather than by an unproved classical trace. No boundary datum outside the specified lift class is assumed attainable; classical boundary regularity, general Neumann lifts and transmission regularity remain later obligations.

exact_citation_checks.quote:
Assume the Axiom of Choice ([[def-axiom-of-choice]]). Let $\Omega$ be a bounded $C^\infty$ domain in $\mathbb R^3$ in the graph sense of [[def-bounded-c-k-domain-and-boundary-charts]]; connectedness is unnecessary. Write $H^m(\Omega)=W^{m,2}(\Omega;\mathbb R)$ with the multi-index integral norm ([[def-sobolev-space-wkp-and-its-norm]]) and $H_0^1(\Omega)$ for the $H^1$ closure of $C_c^\infty(\Omega)$ ([[def-wkp-zero-as-a-sobolev-closure]]). For every real $f\in L^2(\Omega)$ there is a unique $u\in H_0^1(\Omega)\cap H^2(\Omega)$ satisfying

$$\int_\Omega(\nabla u\cdot\nabla v+uv)=\int_\Omega fv\qquad(v\in H_0^1(\Omega)).$$

It satisfies $(1-\Delta)u=f$ distributionally and almost everywhere as an $L^2$ identity, and

$$\|u\|_{H^1(\Omega)}\le\|f\|_{L^2(\Omega)},\qquad\|u\|_{H^2(\Omega)}\le C_\Omega\|f\|_{L^2(\Omega)}.$$

Moreover $D=\{\varphi\in C^\infty(\overline\Omega):\varphi|_{\partial\Omega}=0\}$ is dense in $H^2(\Omega)\cap H_0^1(\Omega)$ in the $H^2$ norm: every such $w$ has $\varphi_j\in D$ with $\varphi_j\to w$ in $H^2$. Here smoothness on the closure means restriction of a smooth function on a neighbourhood of the closure, equivalently the smooth chart representatives used below. In particular $\nabla\varphi_j\to\nabla w$ in the graph norm of $H(\operatorname{curl})\cap H(\operatorname{div})$, with zero curl and $\operatorname{div}\nabla w=\Delta w$; every $\nabla\varphi_j$ is smooth and PEC since its tangential derivatives vanish at the boundary. For precision, let $X_\Omega$ be the graph-norm closure of smooth vector fields on a neighbourhood of the closure with $\nu\times v=0$ on the boundary, where $\nu$ is the outward Euclidean unit normal. The ambient graph space consists of real $L^2$ vector fields whose distributional $\operatorname{div}v=\sum_i\partial_iv_i$ and $\operatorname{curl}v=(\partial_2v_3-\partial_3v_2,\partial_3v_1-\partial_1v_3,\partial_1v_2-\partial_2v_1)$ lie in $L^2$; its norm squared is $\|v\|_2^2+\|\operatorname{curl}v\|_2^2+\|\operatorname{div}v\|_2^2$. Thus $\nabla w$ belongs to this explicitly defined $X_\Omega$, the same completion used by the later cavity item. No equality with every maximal trace realisation is asserted.

No smoothness of $f$, no classical boundary value for general $u$, and no general nonsmooth-domain, Neumann, interface, or variable-coefficient claim is included. Zero boundary condition means membership in $H_0^1$; the published trace theorem identifies its trace as zero.
